title: In a Cohen-Macaulay local ring, elements cutting the dimension by their number form a regular sequence
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (a Noetherian commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$) whose Krull dimension $d=\dim R$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] is finite, and assume that $R$ is Cohen–Macaulay in the sense that $\operatorname{depth}(R)\ge d$ [def-weil-pbc-depth], that is, $\mathfrak m$ contains an $R$-regular sequence of length $d$. Let $c\ge0$ be an integer and $g_1,\dots,g_c\in\mathfrak m$ elements such that the ring $R/(g_1,\dots,g_c)$ has Krull dimension $\dim R/(g_1,\dots,g_c)=d-c$. Then $g_1,\dots,g_c$ is a regular sequence in $R$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence].

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 00N6 (proposition-CM-module, line 25052), first assertion, for the module M = R (the support of R/(g_1,...,g_c) is V(g_1,...,g_c), of dimension dim R/(g_1,...,g_c)); Cohen-Macaulay as in Definition Tag 00N3 (definition-CM, line 24960: dim Supp(M) = depth(M)), here depth(R) >= dim R, equivalent since the depth never exceeds the dimension

proof.text:
(Notation; the quotients as finite $R$-modules.) For $i=0,1,\dots,c$ put $I_i=(g_1,\dots,g_i)\subset R$ (so $I_0=0$) and let $M_i=R/I_i$, a finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] generated by the class of $1$. Since all $g_j\in\mathfrak m$, $I_i\subseteq\mathfrak m
eq R$, so $M_i
eq0$. For $f\in R$, $M_i/fM_i=R/(I_i+fR)$; in particular $M_i/g_{i+1}M_i=M_{i+1}$, and for $M=R$ the module $(g_1,\dots,g_i)M$ of [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] is the ideal $I_i$, so $R/(g_1,\dots,g_i)R=M_i$. The annihilator of $M_i$ is $I_i$ (if $a\cdot ar1=0$ then $a\in I_i$, and $I_i$ kills $R/I_i$), so by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-support-annihilator] $\operatorname{Supp}(M_i)=V(I_i)=\{\mathfrak p:I_i\subseteq\mathfrak p\}$ (localization as in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]). Hence $\operatorname{Supp}(M_i)\cap V(g_{i+1})=V(I_i)\cap V(g_{i+1})=V(I_{i+1})=\operatorname{Supp}(M_{i+1})$. By the correspondence between prime ideals of $R/I_i$ and prime ideals of $R$ containing $I_i$ (which preserves strict inclusions both ways), the chains of primes in $V(I_i)$ are exactly the preimages of the chains of primes of $R/I_i$, so $\delta_i:=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M_i)$ (supremum of lengths of chains of primes in the support) equals the Krull dimension $\dim R/I_i$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. In particular $\delta_0=\dim R=d$ ($\operatorname{Supp}(R)=V(0)=\operatorname{Spec}R$), $\delta_c=d-c$ by hypothesis, and $\delta_i\ge0$ since $M_i
e0$.

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 00N6 (proposition-CM-module, line 25052), proof, first paragraph (lines 25062-25068); 'Let Z = Supp(M)', with M = R and Supp(M/(g_1,...,g_i)M) = Z ∩ V(g_1,...,g_i)

proof.text: (Each $g_{i+1}$ cuts the dimension by exactly one.) For $0\le i<c$, [lem-weil-pbc-support-dimension-quotient-element-bound] applied to the finite $R$-module $M_i$ and $f=g_{i+1}\in\mathfrak m$ gives $\delta_i\le\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M_i/g_{i+1}M_i)+1=\delta_{i+1}+1$ (step 1). Here $\delta_i\ge0$ by step 1. Summing $\delta_j\le\delta_{j+1}+1$ for $j=0,\dots,i-1$ gives $d=\delta_0\le\delta_i+i$, i.e. $\delta_i\ge d-i$; summing it for $j=i,\dots,c-1$ gives $\delta_i\le\delta_c+(c-i)=d-i$ (all $\delta_i$ are finite: $0\le\delta_i\le\delta_0=d$, since $V(I_i)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$). Hence $\delta_i=d-i$ for $i=0,\dots,c$, and so $\dim\bigl(\operatorname{Supp}(M_i)\cap V(g_{i+1})\bigr)=\delta_{i+1}=\delta_i-1$ for $0\le i<c$. (Stacks: 'each step decreases the dimension at most by 1. Hence by assumption each step decreases the dimension by exactly 1 each time.')

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 00N6 (proposition-CM-module, line 25052), proof, first paragraph (lines 25062-25068), 'By Lemma 00KW in the chain Z ⊃ Z ∩ V(g_1) ⊃ ... each step decreases the dimension at most by 1'; the module form of 00KW used here is Lemma Tag 0B52 (lemma-one-equation-module, line 15297), right inequality

proof.text: ($R$ is Cohen–Macaulay as a module over itself.) $R\ne0$ is a finite $R$-module, so [lem-weil-pbc-depth-le-support-dimension] gives $\operatorname{depth}(R)\le\dim\operatorname{Supp}(R)=\delta_0=d$ [def-weil-pbc-depth]. Together with the hypothesis $\operatorname{depth}(R)\ge d$ this gives $\operatorname{depth}(M_0)=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M_0)=d$, i.e. $M_0=R$ is a Cohen–Macaulay module in the sense of Definition Tag 00N3 (the sense used by [lem-weil-pbc-cm-module-good-element-nonzerodivisor]).

source.place: Algebra, Definition Tag 00N3 (definition-CM, line 24960) and Lemma Tag 00LK (lemma-bound-depth, line 17813)

proof.text: (Induction: each $g_{i+1}$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M_i$.) We prove by induction on $i=0,1,\dots,c$ the claim $(C_i)$: $M_i$ is a Cohen–Macaulay $R$-module, i.e. $\operatorname{depth}(M_i)=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M_i)$ $(=d-i)$. $(C_0)$ is step 3. Assume $(C_i)$ with $i<c$. Then $M_i$ is a nonzero finite Cohen–Macaulay module over the Noetherian local ring $R$ (step 1), $g_{i+1}\in\mathfrak m$, and $\dim(\operatorname{Supp}(M_i)\cap V(g_{i+1}))=\dim\operatorname{Supp}(M_i)-1$ (step 2). So [lem-weil-pbc-cm-module-good-element-nonzerodivisor] applies to $M=M_i$, $g=g_{i+1}$: (a) multiplication by $g_{i+1}$ on $M_i$ is injective, and (b) $M_i/g_{i+1}M_i=M_{i+1}$ (step 1) is Cohen–Macaulay, which is $(C_{i+1})$. Hence for every $i=0,\dots,c-1$, $g_{i+1}$ is a nonzerodivisor on $M_i$. (Stacks: 'we may successively apply Lemma 00N5 to the modules M/(g_1,...,g_i) and the element g_{i+1}'.)

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 00N6 (proposition-CM-module, line 25052), proof, first paragraph (lines 25062-25068), 'Thus we may successively apply Lemma 00N5 (lemma-CM-one-g, line 25018) to the modules M/(g_1,...,g_i) and the element g_{i+1}'

proof.text: (Conclusion.) By step 1, $R/(g_1,\dots,g_{i-1})R=M_{i-1}$, on which $g_i$ is a nonzerodivisor for $i=1,\dots,c$ (step 4), and $R/(g_1,\dots,g_c)R=M_c\neq0$ (step 1). These are conditions (1) and (2) of [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] for $M=R$, so $g_1,\dots,g_c$ is a regular sequence in $R$ (for $c=0$ the empty sequence, which is regular since $R\neq0$).
